title: Strict Mode and Errors
story: Scripts should stop on trouble instead of ploughing on. set -e exits on failure and set -u catches typos.
goal: Start with set -eu. If the file in the first argument is missing print error: FILE not found and exit with status 3. Otherwise print Backing up FILE, copy it to FILE.bak and print Done.
hints: exit 3 ends the script with status 3.

set -eu
f="$1"
if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
  echo "error: $f not found"
  exit 3
fi
echo "Backing up $f"
cp "$f" "$f.bak"
echo "Done"
socratic: How does a caller see your exit code?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Strict Mode and Errors”?
solution:
set -eu
f="$1"
if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
  echo "error: $f not found"
  exit 3
fi
echo "Backing up $f"
cp "$f" "$f.bak"
echo "Done"
